title: Lessons
summary: The unit of learning: one job each, one type from a flat list, its own schedule and mastery.
description: Learning happens in lessons. A lesson's type says everything about it: how it is practised, what its page shows, where it goes in a course and what mastering it takes.

stories.want: every lesson to be one small thing with a clear way to do it
stories.soThat: I can fit learning into a few minutes

stories.as: a developer adding a kind of lesson
stories.want: to declare it in one place
stories.soThat: nothing else in the app has to learn about it

stories.want: to see at a glance which lessons are challenges
stories.soThat: a hard one reads as meant to be hard, and I know the course does not need it

requirements.text: Every lesson has exactly one type from the registry, `lesson.types`.

Each type is declared once, with its name, icon, description, how it runs, its place in a course's path and the sections its page shows; the screens draw a lesson from its registry entry, not from its type.
A drill owns its words, sentences or dialogue lines; a study lesson owns its text and objectives.
A word or sentence belongs to exactly one lesson.
Every lesson has a complexity of low, medium or high (shown as quick, medium, deep), which says how long it takes and how deep it goes, not its level.
A lesson's minutes come from one table: drills 2, 4 and 8 for low, medium and high; conversations 5, 10 and 20.
A lesson can carry its own CEFR level; without one it has its course's.
A lesson can be marked a challenge: it does not count toward completing its course, and today's lessons offer it only once the course's other lessons are passed.
A lesson already passed today can be practised again at any time as extra practice.
A new lesson type added to the registry is described to the tutor automatically, from its registry entry.
Every registered type can be made and practised, and every exercise it produces is one the screens can draw; a test fails otherwise.
A challenge is marked as one wherever a lesson is listed or shown: today's lessons and their next lesson, a course's lessons, the lesson's page, and a drill or conversation while it runs.
The mark is the word `term.challenge` with an icon, in `color.challenge`, so it never rests on colour alone.

values.description: Every lesson type, in the order they are offered.

deprecation.reason: Words for concepts are terms now, kept in one place; this one is `term.challenge`.

values.description: The challenge mark: the design system's gold ink.
